correctness.rationale: The determinant transfer can be proved without a separability restriction. In R=F_q[X]/(u) let λ(h) be the top coefficient of the canonical representative, equivalently the X⁻¹ coefficient of h/u. The Hankel matrix from v/u is the matrix of λ(v X^(i+j)), the product of the Gram matrix of λ(X^(i+j)) and the matrix of multiplication by v. The Gram matrix is anti-triangular with unit anti-diagonal, giving ε_n. Multiplication by v has determinant Res(u,v), by triangularizing the companion matrix over an algebraic closure and applying v to it, with repeated roots counted. Thus the Hankel determinant is ε_n times the resultant, including inseparable u. An invertible Hankel matrix determines exactly q pairs: choose the next Laurent coefficient freely, solve for the monic denominator using the nonsingular Hankel system, and recover the numerator as the polynomial part; expanding back produces the original coefficients and the chosen next coefficient. Every such pair is coprime by the determinant identity. For a character of order r, Chinese remaindering over factors P^e gives one local unit sum that vanishes unless r divides e, by surjectivity of the residue-field norm; if r divides e it gives all q^(ed)−q^((e−1)d) units. Consequently the formal series is (1−q^r z^r)/(1−q^(r+1)z^r). Dividing the positive-degree coefficients by q and multiplying by χ(ε_n) gives the claimed transform. The trivial character gives the zero fiber by subtraction, and finite-group character inversion gives the Ramanujan sums and the iff uniformity criterion. This includes n=1, q=2 and the cases where the characteristic divides n.
residual_risks: The recorded enumeration was not independently replayed; the all-parameter result is verified by proof. The conclusion is for square Hankel matrices over fields, not general rings.

evidence: Appendix Lemma A.1, over any field, writes each pointed rational function uniquely in terms of monic P_i with positive degrees n_i summing to n, and constants a_i≠0, giving resultant σ(n_i)∏a_i^n_i.
Remark A.2 gives σ=1 when all n_i are even. Theorem A.5 gives the resultant-1 point count for all n and q, whereas Corollary 1.4 has p∤n.
The Hankel rank theorems give the total invertible or determinant-zero count; they do not supply the multiplicative spectrum by themselves.
broader_coverage.reasoning: It is the stronger structural lemma in the appendix, not just the special resultant-1 theorem, that covers all nonzero values with no tame-characteristic restriction.

evidence: At a composition (n_1,...,n_k), apply χ to the monomial and sum independently over each a_i. Orthogonality kills the composition unless r divides all n_i. On survivors χ(σ)=1: for r odd χ(−1)=1, and for r even all n_i are even, so σ=1 by Remark A.2.

There are q^n choices of P_i for each composition. For r|n the surviving compositions of length k are counted by binomial(n/r−1,k−1), so their moments sum to q^n∑_k binomial(n/r−1,k−1)(q−1)^k=(q−1)q^(n+n/r−1); if r does not divide n there are none.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior monomial description and the binomial theorem already produce exactly the frozen all-size resultant spectrum. The signed q-to-one transfer gives the claimed Hankel transform, and standard inversion then gives every fiber and the uniformity criterion. There is no uncovered range when p divides n.
searches: Cazanave Appendix Lemma A.1 and Remark A.2, published PDF pp. 348–350

evidence: The signed q-to-one transfer identifies Hankel determinant t with coprime pointed rational functions A/B of resultant ε_n t, counted with multiplicity q. Replacing the lower-degree member B by B+A also relates this space to pairs of monic degree-n polynomials with the same resultant (in the ordering with A first).
Cazanave directly decomposes the coprime pointed rational functions by ordered compositions and a signed monomial resultant.
Row reversal identifies Hankel and Toeplitz fibers with determinant sign ε_n.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Exact resultant character moments are equivalent to the Hankel transform up to the single factor q⁻¹χ(ε_n); the transfer preserves arbitrary nonzero determinant levels, not just nonsingularity.

This is established by an exact character evaluation on the prior decomposition, not by a matching title or by the fixed-size table alone. The zero fiber was already a standard rank count. The norm/Euler-product argument is a different derivation, not a distinct determinant-fiber theorem.

value.rationale: The nonzero determinant distribution is a natural question, but as a proposed new exact classification the frozen result re-expresses data already determined by the prior resultant parametrization. The character-order cutoff and uniformity criterion are direct consequences of that same data, and no additional distributional consequence beyond it is established. The alternate norm/Euler-product proof may be useful exposition, but the submitted record does not establish an independent improvement or application that would support a different valuable claim.
residual_risks: No assessment is made of a new application of the Euler-product method outside this already determined family.
